page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processor clocked at 3.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES cryptography, and BMI2. It has no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and does not include discrete GPUs. Network throughput is provisioned with a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Across standardized benchmark suites, the ecs.g7ne.8xlarge consistently ranks in the average range for its hardware category. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1358.0 and a multi-core score of 11662.0, with a Clang compilation score of 25676.0. Synthetic compute evaluation via stress-ng registers 1576.79 for single-core and 33292.22 for multi-core performance. In memory metrics, the instance registers 114.67 GB/sec large-block uncached read bandwidth and 53.49 GB/sec write bandwidth, supported by a PassMark memory score of 2732.95. Application-level measurements demonstrate 31.14 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 23.96 GB/sec.

The balanced compute-to-memory distribution combined with dedicated 3.3 GHz cores and 25 Gbps networking positions the instance for enterprise web applications, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and memory-backed caching layers like Redis. However, because the instance includes no local ephemeral storage, workloads with intensive local disk IOPS requirements will rely entirely on remote network storage, introducing network storage latency considerations.

The platform provides 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and supports instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions and AES. The instance contains no local SSD storage and lacks GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard compute engines, backed by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic testing places its processing and memory performance squarely in the mid-range bracket, featuring a multi-core Geekbench score of 11662.0 and Redis performance of 31.14 million operations per second. This profile makes ecs.g7ne.8xlarge suited for scalable web tiers, application backends, mid-sized caching clusters, and automated build environments.
